newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA JIANSHE SEES SLIGHTLY HIGHER H1 NET.
newsitem.headline: CHINA JIANSHE SEES SLIGHTLY HIGHER H1 NET.

text.p: China's Shenzhen North Jianshe Motorcycle Co Ltd expects a modest rise in its 1997 interim net profit from 48.31 million yuan in the first half of 1996, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
The estimate was based on international accounting standards.

Earnings edged up in January-June 1997 because of marginally higher motorcycle output and sales, the spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin. Motorcycle sale prices held steady in the first half, he added.
Jianshe's first-half 1996 sales stood at 1.13 billion yuan.
The company, one of China's leading motorcycle producers, cut its sale prices by an average 10 percent in late 1995 to compete with domestic rivals. Prices have changed little since.
The firm, which has production facilities in southwestern Sichuan province but has its headquarters in Shenzhen, produced about 335,000 motorcycles in the first six months of last year.
Output reached 578,335 motorcycles in 1996, although it sold a total of 608,626 last year. The company will publish its 1997 interim results in the near future, the official said.

North Jianshe posted net profit of 50.73 million yuan for 1996, compared with 288.71 million in 1995 under international accounting standards. The company attributed the earnings plunge to sharply lower sales as a result of weak demand and decreased prices.

The company's sales were 2.49 billion yuan in 1996 against 3.61 billion yuan the previous year. China North Industrial Group, a major state-owned conglomerate, has a controlling stake in North Jianshe.
The Beijing-based group controls more than 150 enterprises involved in a wide range of products including munitions, machinery and chemicals.
The group also has controlling stakes in three other firms listed on the Shanghai or Shenzhen stock exchanges, some directly and some in the names of other companies.
They are Chongqing Changan Automobile Co Ltd 2625.SZ, motorcycle maker China Jialing Industrial Co Ltd and Chengdu Tianxing Instrument and Meter Co Ltd.
